key_insight: Reward models inherit representational value biases from their pretrained LLM initializations: across 10 open-weight RMs and validated psycholinguistic corpora, RMs show consistent, systematic value and social biases traceable to pretraining.
problem_solved: Identifies and quantifies how pretrained LLM representations shape reward-model judgments, filling a gap in understanding why RMs can reflect undesired value biases even after alignment training.
method: Evaluate 10 leading open-weight RMs on validated psycholinguistic corpora probing moral, political, and social attitudes.
Measure bias and preference signals per RM and compute correlations with features of their pretrained LLMs (architecture, pretraining corpora, representation signatures).
Use controlled analyses (comparative metrics and ablations) to attribute observed RM biases to pretraining factors rather than only fine-tuning procedures.
impact: Shows that alignment efforts must consider pretrained representations when designing and auditing reward models; practitioners should test and mitigate inherited value biases before deploying RMs in downstream alignment or RLHF pipelines.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing bias scores across the 10 RMs for several psycholinguistic measures (e.g., moral valence, political leaning, stereotype strength).
Heatmap/correlation matrix linking RM bias measures to pretraining corpus attributes and model architecture features.
Pipeline diagram showing flow: pretrained LLM → RM initialization → reward fine-tuning → observed biases, annotated with where inheritance occurs.
Small vignette examples: paired prompts and RM preferences illustrating concrete biased outputs.
paper_title: Reward Models Inherit Value Biases from Pretraining
paper_authors: Brian Christian, Jessica A. F. Thompson, Elle Michelle Yang, Vincent Adam, Hannah Rose Kirk
